crossRepoLiteralDrift.theDeadEndWorthRecording: Pointing --ldt-root at P:/legacy-design-tools (the main checkout on this machine) REFUSES: `{"error":"DRIFT_MARKER_MISSING: const PLANNED_DEVELOPMENT_PATTERN not found","code":"DRIFT_MARKER_MISSING"}`, exit 2. That checkout's working tree predates P-257's move of the const, and the checker reads the sibling's WORKING TREE first and only then `git show HEAD:path` -- so a stale sibling checkout reads as cross-repo drift. It is not drift; it is a stale tree. Use a fresh checkout or a scratch worktree at origin/main.
crossRepoLiteralDrift.whyThisLaneDoesNotAddItsRow: SETBACK_SOURCE_CONFLICT_NOTE / _TOKEN are new pinned literals with honest cross-repo copies (each file says so), but a row that reads a file the sibling's MAIN does not have yet REFUSES (exit 2) on EVERY PR -- which is exactly what the checker's own header says at lines 48-53 about its own script and about P-270's address fixture. Both halves of this lane are unmerged, so the sibling main lacks the file in both directions: adding the row in the map PR would refuse on the LDT side, and adding it in the LDT PR would refuse on the map side. The row is therefore named for the sync PR in the close, exactly as P-270's was.

threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenTheyDisagree: setback-card-route-divergence.test.ts (card) and setbackDivergenceP340.test.ts (route) pin the same 7 tuples from the same measured fixture; the falsifier above shows each fails when its own side's table is moved alone. The card additionally pins the SERVED payload (setback-card-serve-p340.test.ts), so a resolution that is right but not served is also a failure.
whatBypassesIt: THE BAKE'S STORED VALUES: a parcel served from an already-baked envelope never reaches either resolver, so a re-bake is what carries this change to the surface; until then the old tuples keep serving. This is the bypass the dispatch itself names.

A SURFACE THAT RESOLVES SETBACKS OUTSIDE THE SHARED PACKAGE: searched for and NOT FOUND on these two paths -- the retired card module was the only one, and it is now deleted with a guard test. The guard walks the app's whole source tree; it does not cover other repos.

THE MCP HALF (P-339) and the factory's setback-row writers (P-354 #179, P-300/P-338): out of this lane's scope by the dispatch. If any of them composes its own table home, it is a surface this lane's divergence test cannot see.

NO CANDIDATE AT ALL: when neither a corpus row nor a usable atom rule exists (or a per-parcel-only jurisdiction such as bastrop-city-tx has no record), resolveCardSetbacks returns null and the CALLER's decline logic applies -- there is no longer a vendored table to fall back to, which is the point of the retirement. A jurisdiction the corpus does not publish therefore declines or serves the atom rule with no table citation, where the old card would have consulted its own 4-file subset.
A LITERAL NOBODY LISTED IN P-331'S TABLE: the new conflict-row literals are not pinned cross-repo yet, by the ordering constraint argued above.

findingsAndLessons.LESSON: A card/route disagreement can be a MISSING TABLE rather than a wrong value: on 5 of these 7 subjects the card had no table for that city at all (its vendored SETBACK_TABLES held 4 jurisdictions) and served the bake snapshot while the route read a codified row. Comparing the two tables' values finds nothing when one side has no row; compare the two SOURCE KINDS and the jurisdiction coverage first.

The corner axis is the axis most likely to be lost silently: an adapter that emits `side_corner_ft` only when it differs from the side yard drops a real standard whenever the two are equal, and the served '-' looks like an honest absence. All 5 of this lane's axis defects had corner == side in the atom.

The cross-repo drift checker reads the sibling's WORKING TREE before its HEAD, so a stale sibling checkout produces DRIFT_MARKER_MISSING (exit 2) that looks like drift and is not. Use a scratch worktree at origin/main to reproduce CI.
findingsAndLessons.DEAD_END: Looking for LDT's copy of the drift checker with `Select-String -SimpleMatch 'cross-repo|literal-drift'` returns nothing because -SimpleMatch treats the pipe as a literal; and the LDT workflow file was absent locally because LDT main had advanced mid-lane. Re-fetch before concluding a file does not exist -- the first conclusion here was wrong and the CI run proved it.
